mechanism_narrative: A sustained downward trend in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market and weak economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0%) despite negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) combined with a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a hawkish monetary policy stance that compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in the interaction regime are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a post-crisis recovery regime (UNRATE < 5.0%), rising housing starts (HOUST) signal strengthening demand for residential construction, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% and HOUST is rising, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which supports corporate profits and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in rising INDPRO periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates weakening labor market conditions and reduced consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in declining PAYEMS periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), an increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals improving labor market conditions and economic recovery, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS rising), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
